subject: Cost & pricing follow-up: token volumes, latency trade-offs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@fintechai.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps — token volumes / latency trade-offs

Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so we can size cost/latency options for the integration: 

- Estimated monthly token volumes you mentioned: 500M - 2B tokens (depending on adoption / staged rollout). I logged a conservative plan at 1B tokens/mo for initial sizing.
- Primary latency SLO: 300ms p95 for user-facing endpoints; for some async batch tasks 2-3s is fine.
- Key trade-off: you said cost sensitivity is high (budget range: $5k–$20k/month initially), but you also want predictable SLAs for the pilot.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Can you confirm a more concrete monthly token target for pilot (low/expected/high)? (I attached a quick token estimate template.)
2) I'll loop Marcus (pricing lead) to outline 2 pricing options: 
   - Low-latency tier (p95 ~200-300ms): higher $/1M tokens due to reserved capacity and lower bin-packing.
   - Cost-optimized tier (streaming + batching, p95 ~500-800ms): lower $/1M tokens but higher tail latency.
3) We can provide a target unit-economics example (target $/1M tokens) matched to your budget scenarios.

Attachments: fintechai_token_estimates.xlsx (please fill the "expected" column), redwood_pricing_tiers_v2.pdf (high-level tiers).

Happy to jump on a 20-min call if you'd like Marcus to walk the pricing options.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — token volumes / latency trade-offs

Thanks Marissa — that looks great. Quick answers: 
- For the pilot we expect: low 500M / expected 1.2B / high 2B tokens per month. Priya is the PM and will help refine.
- Budget: initial pilot budget target is $10k–$15k/month; we'd need to show path to <$5k/month net unit cost at scale.
- Latency: 300ms p95 is the goal for user-facing, but we can accept higher for some non-critical flows.

Yes please have Marcus share the two options. I'm fine with a short call — Wed or Thu afternoon PT works.

Best,

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@fintechai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — token volumes / latency trade-offs

Alex / Team — thanks for the details. I sketched two concrete pricing scenarios and unit economics. High-level notes below; see attached mutual_action_plan.docx for timeline & milestones.

Scenario A — Low-latency (reserved capacity / Dedicated-style profile)
- Expected p95: ~200–300ms for user endpoints (with pinned capacity).
- Recommended configuration: Dedicated tier w/ reserved GPU pool, 4 concurrent workers, small batching (batch window ~10–20ms), streaming enabled for interactive responses.
- Cost estimate (1.2B tokens/mo): ~ $18k/month (~$15.0 / 1M tokens).
- Pros: predictable latency and throughput, simpler SLAs. Cons: higher baseline spend; less flexible for large traffic variance.

Scenario B — Cost-optimized (streaming + larger batching / autoscale)
- Expected p95: ~450–700ms depending on batching profile; median latency remains low because of streaming, but tail increases.
- Recommended configuration: Hosted tier w/ adaptive batching, KV/prefix caching for repeated prompts, aggressive token-level caching for templates.
- Cost estimate (1.2B tokens/mo): ~ $8.5k/month (~$7.1 / 1M tokens).
- Pros: Lower unit cost, better for unpredictable volume and bursty traffic. Cons: higher p95 tail, requires SLO testing and fallbacks for critical paths.

Unit economics examples: we modeled target $/1M token thresholds at $5, $10, $15 to map to budget bands. For pilots targeting $10k–$15k we can offer a blended plan and a short-term credit to bridge (details in the attached).

Questions for you: 
- Which user flows must hit the 300ms p95? (Login/checkout vs. background enrichment?)
- Any hard budget floor we should not exceed during the pilot? (Alex said $10k–$15k target.)

If helpful, we can produce a SLO-driven pricing proposal where we map two SKU tiers to latency buckets and provide a fallback discount if p95 is missed during the pilot window. Happy to review on our Wed call — when exactly is good for you?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex@fintechai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@fintechai.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps — token volumes / latency trade-offs

Marcus — this is super helpful, thanks. A couple of clarifications before the call: 

1) Critical flows: authentication prompts and checkout flow need to be <=300ms p95. Everything else (recommendations, batch enrichment) can be 500–800ms.
2) Pilot budget hard cap: $18k/month; target comfortable band is $10k–$15k. We need a path to <$5k/1M at scale.

SLO-driven pricing question: we'd be interested in a model where you expose two SKUs (low-latency & cost-optimized) and you provide credits if latency targets for the low-latency SKU are missed during the pilot. On the call can you: 
- Walk through how batching/window sizes impact tail latency (and what defaults Redwood recommends).
- Show an example billing cadence for the two SKUs and a sample blended bill for our expected 1.2B tokens.
- Confirm whether streaming + caching is compatible with the low-latency SKU or only with cost-optimized.

I filled the expected column in the attached token estimate and re-uploaded it (see fintechai_token_estimates.xlsx). Can we meet Wed 11/12 at 2:30pm PT?

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product | FintechAI
alex@fintechai.com
